content: Saga pattern: distributed operations across independently owned databases are broken into a sequence of local transactions, each publishing an event/message that triggers the next step. Failure at any step is resolved via compensating transactions that logically (not physically) reverse prior steps. Both the forward steps and the compensating actions MUST be idempotent and safely retryable, since sagas trade strong consistency (2PC) for availability/eventual consistency -- there is no distributed lock across the two databases.
